title: Horizon and Current
premise: Astrid Villalobos inherits his estranged father's compass and a map fragment pointing to the San Telmo, a wrecked treasure galleon upriver in the delta — along with his father's debts to the ruthless salvage magnate Corvo. When the father's expedition goes silent, Astrid joins a rival crew racing six tides ahead of Corvo's fleet, guided by the compass's strange pull and by Marisol, the expedition's radio operator who knows more than she says. Betrayals strip both crews down to a handful of believers, and Astrid must choose between claiming the wreck to pay his debt or destroying it to keep it from Corvo. In the end he scuttles the treasure into the deep, settles his debt with truth instead of gold, and chooses love over inheritance.
about_author: Gideon Okafor is a former river pilot turned novelist who spent a decade running cargo through tidal deltas before trading charts for manuscripts. He writes adventure stories about people whose loyalties run deeper than their maps.

chapters.title: The Weight of Brass
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In a portside pawnshop, Astrid pawns his last instrument but keeps his dead father's compass, which he cannot bring himself to sell. A debt collector finds him: Corvo holds his father's notes, due within weeks. Emotional beat: resentment braided with grief.

chapters.title: Six Tides of Silence
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. News breaks that his father's expedition upriver has stopped answering its radio. That night the compass needle swings toward the delta on its own. Astrid decides to go — not for his father, he tells himself, but for the wreck that could erase his debt. Beat: reluctant commitment.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He signs aboard the Perla, a scrappy salvage sloop captained by the pragmatic Odalys Reyes. He meets Marisol, the quiet radio operator who was the last voice to hear his father's expedition. Beat: wary alliance; first spark of trust.

chapters.title: What the Radio Kept
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She plays Astrid his father's final transmissions: not distress, but a warning — 'Corvo knows.' She admits she withheld this, fearing he'd refuse the voyage. Beat: betrayal and forgiveness in one breath; they bind themselves to each other.

chapters.title: Downstream of the Law
chapters.summary: Odalys's POV. The Perla slips past the customs cutter at night; the wreck lies outside any nation's waters, where salvage law is whatever you can enforce. Odalys explains her stake: her brother died on Corvo's last expedition. Beat: the theme of justice outside the law takes hold.

chapters.title: First Tide
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Racing Corvo's lead ship, the Venganza, the Perla cuts through the mangrove maze using the compass as a guide. They find the first marker buoy smashed — someone got here before them. Beat: dread; the race is closer than anyone admitted.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Sheltering in a half-submerged settlement, the crew learns from an old ferryman that Corvo's men bought supplies days ago — and took hostages among the villagers. Astrid wants to push on; Odalys turns back to help. Beat: duty versus the clock.

chapters.title: Second Tide
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The rescue costs them half a tide and their engineer, who stays behind to guard the freed villagers. Astrid rages at the delay until Marisol shows him the compass trembling — the wreck is near. Beat: cost of conscience made real.

chapters.title: Corvo's Table
chapters.summary: Villain POV (Corvo). Aboard the Venganza, Corvo dines with a bribed harbormaster and reveals he engineered the father's debt to force him to find the wreck. He learns the Perla is ahead. Beat: cold menace; the antagonist becomes personal.

chapters.title: Third Tide
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Night dive on a false target — a decoy wreck planted by his own father to mislead salvagers. Among the bones of the decoy, Astrid finds a sealed tin: his father's true chart and an apology never sent. Beat: grief cracking open into understanding.

chapters.title: Love Against the Chart
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Astrid and Marisol decode the chart together through a storm-bound night, close as two people can be without saying it. She confesses she loved his father like family and failed him. Beat: tenderness amid rising water; the romance anchors.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide
chapters.summary: Odalys's POV. The Venganza gains on them; Odalys runs the Perla through a rapids shortcut that nearly kills them all. Her brother's death is revealed: Corvo cut the lifeline to save the cargo. Beat: vengeance sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Mutiny Question
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Two crewmen argue for turning back — the wreck may be cursed, the odds suicidal. Astrid, now de facto leader, must hold them with something better than gold: the promise that no one else dies for Corvo's ledger. Beat: leadership forged under fracture.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They reach the lagoon where the San Telmo sleeps beneath sixty feet of black water. Marisol sends a false radio signal to lure the Venganza wide. It works — too well; Corvo suspects a trap and sends armed divers ahead. Beat: triumph shadowed by escalation.

chapters.title: Into the Hold
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. First descent: Astrid swims the flooded galleon's hold and finds the treasure intact — and his father's body beside it, dead not of greed but protecting the decoy secret. Beat: the emotional climax of grief; the debt suddenly means nothing.

chapters.title: Blood in the Lagoon
chapters.summary: Odalys's POV. Corvo's divers attack; a firefight erupts across the lagoon at dawn. Odalys gets her reckoning with Corvo's lieutenant and pays for it with a wound. Beat: violence with consequence; the lawless world exacts its price.

chapters.title: The Choice at Six Tides
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. With the Venganza entering the lagoon, Astrid holds the detonator over the charges rigged to collapse the wreck into the trench. Gold would free him; destruction would free everyone. Beat: the novel's moral fulcrum, held at maximum tension.

chapters.title: What Sinks, What Rises
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid fires the charges; the San Telmo folds into the deep as Corvo watches his fortune vanish. Enraged, Corvo boards the Perla for revenge. Beat: catharsis immediately menaced; no clean victory.

chapters.title: Compass Point
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. Hand-to-hand struggle on the tilting deck; the compass falls between them. Marisol's radio call finally brings the customs cutter — justice arrives late, but arrives. Odalys corners Corvo; Astrid chooses capture over killing. Beat: justice chosen over vengeance.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In port, Astrid faces Corvo's creditors with the truth: the debt dies with the treasure, and the courts take Corvo instead. He keeps only the compass and his father's letter. Beat: release; inheritance redefined as memory, not money.

chapters.title: Anchorage
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol and Astrid repair the Perla together, deciding neither will sail alone again. Odalys offers them permanent berths; the found crew becomes a found family. Beat: warmth after wreckage; love settled against duty resolved.

chapters.title: Horizon and Current
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, epilogue. A year later, Astrid dives the empty trench where the galleon lay and leaves his father's compass on the sand — then surfaces to Marisol and open water. Some inheritances are meant to be given back. Beat: peace; the horizon finally wider than the debt.
